title: Austin Plans Streets, Paving, and Presidential Visit
summary:
• **Infrastructure Investments**: The council approved multiple street improvement projects totaling over $5,000, including $4,530 for paving Congress Avenue and 7th-8th Streets with creosote, plus water main upgrades and storm drainage improvements.

• **Railroad Expansion Approved**: The council granted two railroad companies permission to extend their tracks on 8th and 24th Streets, with a requirement that the railroad maintain the streets in good repair.

• **Presidential Invitation**: Austin officially invited President Theodore Roosevelt to visit the capital city, with the mayor authorized to send an engraved invitation to Washington for presentation to the president.

• **Government Operations**: The council approved salary appropriations totaling over $10,000 to cover city employees, officers, aldermen, and street teams through the end of 1905.

• **Community Development**: The council authorized $200 to open a new street in South Austin and $250 for extra sidewalk and street labor, reflecting city growth in residential areas.

Resolution inviting Alderman Nitschke offered the following President U.S. to resolution,
which was read and adopted Visit Austin Whereas reliable information has been received
that his Excellency, the President of the United States, the Honorable Theodore Roosevelt
contemplates visiting the state of Texas in the latter part of March, or April, 1905, and
Whereas, the people of Texas, from the Red River to the Gufp, from the Sabine to the Rio
Grande, are most earnestly desirous of the opportunity of receiving the Chief Magistrate
of this great Republic in our state, therefore Be it Resolved, by the City Council of the
City of Austin, Texas, that we, in the names of all of the people of Austin, extend to
President Roosevelt and party, a most hearty and sincere invitation to visit the Capital
City of Texas, and assure him a most cordial welcome at the hands of our people, and Be it
further resolved, that these resolutions be duly spread upon the minutes of the City
Council, and that the Mayor, the Honorable R. E. While, and is hereby authorized and
directed to cause a copy of the same to be engrossed and forwarded to the Honorable A. S.
Dunley, at Washington with the request that he present the same to the President.
Respectfully Submitted
H. B. Nitschke
Alderman 5th Ward
